question: Every v4 'not_in_data' case triaged to (a) fetch, (b) proxy, (c) absent
rule: Shivam, 30 Oct 2026: 'not in data' is not an acceptable answer by itself.

inputs.sandbox_network: Outbound network is unavailable in this sandbox (web_search has no key; TLS fetch fails). A source is marked verified when the exact feed is already held (rows in our stores) or the URL is a live constant in an existing fetcher; no live HEAD check was possible.

method.case_source: rebuilt the v4 registry in memory with build_concept_registry.build() (897 mapped / 150 NID / 26 unmapped reproduced exactly), so every case id and its registry reason is the registry's own.
method.grouping: grouped by TRUE missing atom and ask shape, not by registry reason; each case has exactly one class.
method.verdict_rule: a = the atom is held or fetchable free in <=1 day and the answer is a fact/computation; b = the atom is not published and the answer needs a proxy formula or a labelled assumption; c = neither.
method.caveat: A case can be unlocked by an (a) atom and still need a labelled view; the verdict describes the DATA, not the reasoning layer.

source.name: NSE integrated XBRL result filings (held)

classes.label: Rate change -> NIM / credit cost / deposit repricing

proxy.recipe: NIM_q = (InterestEarned_q - InterestExpended_q) / avg(Advances + Investments) x 4; credit_cost_q = ProvisionsOtherThanTaxAndContingencies_q / avg(Advances); deposit repricing from the AR deposit schedule (savings/term split); the repricing order (EBLR -> MCLR -> fixed) from the AR/deck disclosure
proxy.assumption: quarter-end balances approximate averages; the disclosed NIM includes CRR/SLR and other earning assets, so the computed series is a proxy, not the reported number
proxy.confidence: medium-high (NIM within ~10-15% of reported; credit cost medium)
proxy.worked_example: MB0931 HDFC Bank Q2FY27: InterestEarned_q 83,427 cr - InterestExpended_q 48,807 cr = NII 34,619 cr; earning assets = Advances 33.16 lakh cr + Investments 13.57 lakh cr = 46.73 lakh cr; NIM = 34,619/4,673,000 x 4 = 2.96% annualised on quarter-end balances. The one-off leg is RevenueOnInvestments vs OtherIncome in the same filing; if the treasury delta is more than half the NIM delta, label the expansion one-off.

source.format: daily zip/CSV per underlying/expiry/strike/option_type: oi, oi_change, volume, settle

classes.notes: Registry reason said 'paid-only consensus'. It is neither paid nor missing: OI is held. The interpretation (ceiling vs hedge) is a labelled view.

proxy.recipe: for each hop, cross-correlate the held monthly series (World Bank Pink Sheet: wb_gold, wb_rubber, wb_crude_brent, wb_urea, wb_natgas_*, wb_coal_*, wb_cotton_a, wb_dap, wb_iron_ore) against the company metric at lags 0-4 quarters; report the lag that maximises |correlation| and its sample size; the hop with no held series is stated as an assumption, not measured
proxy.assumption: monthly commodity averages map to the quarter they fall in; policy dates are policy_events.effective_date; unmeasured hops are labelled
proxy.confidence: medium-low (direction often clear, magnitude and lag usually not)
proxy.worked_example: MB0460 (gold 2,028 -> 4,186.7, 7 Aug 2020 to 30 Sep 2026): TITAN adjusted close 1,091.05 -> 4,587 (+320%, 26.3% CAGR) vs MUTHOOTFIN 1,217 -> 2,737.1 (+125%, 14.1% CAGR). Price says the jeweller won, not the gold-loan NBFC; the answer must name the channel (gold -> jewellery revenue vs gold -> LTV/AUM) and say that gold alone explains neither, so the pass-through is an assumption.

proxy.recipe: free_float = shares_out x (1 - promoter_pct/100); float_mcap = free_float x close; weight_i = float_mcap_i / sum(float_mcap) over the index's members at that date (company_membership_pit added_on/removed_on); a promoter sale of k pp multiplies the weight by (100 - P + k)/(100 - P)
proxy.assumption: float-weighted index with no capping band; promoter % at the last quarter-end before the event
proxy.confidence: high for free float and direction, medium for the absolute weight (index capping and banding not modelled)
proxy.worked_example: MB0738 (promoter sells 8% via OFS): MUTHOOTFIN promoter 73.35%, public 26.65% (company_ownership_pit 2026-06-30). After an 8 pp OFS the float goes 26.65% -> 34.65%, a 1.30x relative increase; a float-weighted index weight rises ~1.30x before capping. Answer: float up, weight up, and the price reaction is a flow question the data cannot separate from the sale's information content.

proxy.recipe: securitised_share = securitisation_income / (securitisation_income + interest_income) from the AR note, or 'loans assigned' / disbursements from the PPT; rank HFCs by that share; guard: net NPA from results_xbrl PercentageOfNpa, delta <= 2 pp
proxy.assumption: securitisation income is proportional to the securitised book (same yield across HFCs)
proxy.confidence: medium-low (income-to-book ratio is an imperfect proxy for disbursement share)
proxy.worked_example: MB0141 Can Fin Homes Q1FY27: the net-NPA leg is exact from XBRL (PercentageOfNpa); the securitised share is read from the Q1FY27 investor presentation (held deck, securitisation/assignment slide). Answer form: 'Can Fin net NPA x% (XBRL filing f); securitised share y% of disbursements (PPT p.n); guard passes/fails by z pp', with the securitised share labelled an estimate. The deck text search currently finds no securitisation passage, so this needs a targeted page extraction first.

classes.label: JV / subsidiary terms, timing and capital

source.name: BSE announcements + concall + deck (held)
source.format: announcement headlines/attachments + cc_items + deck facts; JV terms as dates/amounts/conditions

classes.notes: Cochin Shipyard ISRF / Dixon-Vivo: terms are in Reg-30 announcements and concall; no new feed. 'Firm order vs JV optionality' is a labelled view over the extracted terms.

classes.label: Valuation / capital-allocation judgement
classes.target_table: formula layer (PB/ROE, payout, FCF) over held financials + guidance

proxy.recipe: state the arithmetic: g_implied from PB = (ROE - g)/(r - g) with r = 12% and ROE = 3-yr average; payout = (CFO - capex)/dividends; premium to book = PB vs ROE; then compare with the company's own guidance (concall_facts) and its delivered trend, not consensus
proxy.assumption: cost of equity 12%; sustainable ROE from the 3-yr average; no analyst consensus (Shivam 2026-10-19: consensus is a guess, use guidance instead)
proxy.confidence: low-medium (a labelled view, never a 'fair value')
proxy.worked_example: MB1010 Power Grid: payout = regulated equity x allowed RoE x (1 - capex share of regulated equity). If the capex cycle slows, regulated equity growth slows and the same RoE supports a higher payout mechanically; the answer gives the payout range at the last five years' capex intensity and labels the regulated-return assumption.

classes.label: Testable delivery / 52-week-high hypotheses
classes.missing_atom: no atom missing; statistic over held prices

source.name: daily_price_delivery + truth px_*_adj (held)
source.format: date, symbol, close, delivery_pct, 52w high; event windows and forward returns

classes.notes: These are measurements, not forecasts: the question asks whether high delivery predicts, so the answer is a hit-rate / IC with a sample size. The existing harness does walk-forward scoring.

proxy.recipe: float_income = average client funding book x 91-day T-bill/yield; client funding book from the AR 'client funding' note (or 'balances with clearing corporation'); cross-check against interest income; report the estimate as a range
proxy.assumption: client float is invested at the short rate and the book is stable through the quarter
proxy.worked_example: MB0483 Angel One: 2023-04-21 transcript p.25, management (Vineet Agrawal): 'We are not disclosing the breakup of the float income and the interest income, which we earn from client funding book yet.' So the share is a proxy: client funding book x short rate; the answer must label it an estimate and say the company does not disclose it.

classes.label: Retail mark-to-market loss on a day

proxy.recipe: retail_loss = sum over ISINs of (public_pct - fii_pct - dii_pct) x shares_out x delta_price; where FII/DII are missing use public_pct and report an upper bound
proxy.assumption: quarter-end ownership applied to that day's price change; public % includes institutions when the split is missing
proxy.confidence: low-medium (upper bound, not a measured loss)
proxy.worked_example: MB0629 (4 Jun 2024): public (non-promoter) holding value is Rs 8.99 lakh crore across 1,724 matched ISINs in company_state_daily x company_ownership_pit; Nifty fell 5.9% that day, so the upper bound is ~Rs 53,000 crore. The answer must say it is an upper bound because public includes FII/DII where the split is null.

proxy.recipe: curated edge supplier -> customer/segment from AR related-party and customer-concentration notes + 'award of order' announcements that name the buyer; evidence bar = a filing naming the relationship; size only where the order value is filed
proxy.assumption: a named relationship implies revenue exposure; unlisted intermediaries are skipped
proxy.confidence: medium for who is in the chain, low for the size
proxy.worked_example: MB0512 (BEL/HAL indigenisation): the second layer is only names with a filing that names a defence programme or PSU customer (e.g. a 'receipt of order from BEL' announcement). Answer: list the names with the filing date and order value, and say plainly which links are inferred from sector membership rather than a named order.

classes.label: Policy incidence: who is hit first and second

proxy.recipe: first hit = companies whose cost-of-materials line contains the taxed input (cogs split from company_cost_structure); second = their customers by sector input share; the policy row comes from policy_events with effective_date and amount
proxy.assumption: input-cost shares are the transmission weights; no firm-level pass-through coefficient
proxy.worked_example: MB0513 (TCS on coal and iron ore doubles to 2% from 1 Apr 2026): first hit = coal/iron-ore producers and steel/cement (coal is in cogs); second = power and steel users. Answer: name the policy_events row, the first-layer cogs exposures, and label the second layer as an input-share estimate, not a measured pass-through.

classes.label: Debt maturity profile

source.name: AR borrowings-maturity note (ar_facts)
source.format: maturity buckets (<1y, 1-3y, 3-5y, >5y) with secured/unsecured split

classes.notes: SCHEMA_FINAL row 10 prices the mix table at 3.5 h; Vedanta's note is the case.

proxy.recipe: show the arithmetic of a doubling: a mid-cap at 20x with 18% earnings growth needs ~40x, or a 100% earnings beat, in 12 months; give a range and the assumptions, never a single name as a fact
proxy.assumption: multiple and earnings paths are scenarios, not predictions
proxy.worked_example: MB0627 ('which mid-cap will double in 2027?'): answer with the two paths (re-rating vs earnings) and the screen that would produce candidates, and state that any single name is a scenario. SCHEMA_FINAL section 4 marks this kind as NOT IN DATA with a labelled view.

source.name: BSE 'Award of Order / Receipt of Order' announcements + order_alert events (164)
source.format: headline + attachment: customer, value, execution period

classes.notes: theme_map is 0 rows, so the theme leg must be curated (20 min). Green hydrogen second layer = companies whose filing names a green-hydrogen order, not sector labels.
